topic: Fourth-order minimax randomization for a single fixed impulse-response path. For Y_t=sum_{l=0}^{K-1}g_l x_{t-l}+e_t, globally sign-symmetric pairwise-orthogonal binary assignment, and the joint ellipsoid ||g||^2/R_g^2+||e||^2/(T R_e^2)<=1, characterize the exact design-based minimax MSE of the unbiased moment estimator. Prove for K=2 and q=e_0 that V_{T,2}=max{R_e^2,a_T R_g^2/T}, a_T=1 for even T and 2 for odd T, with all optimizer membership conditions, explicit mirrored-edge-sign attaining laws, and matching algebraic dual/parity certificates. For fixed K,q, prove equality of finite-horizon and stationary limits and construct pairwise-orthogonal finite-state randomized Golay-block laws attaining R_e^2 max_{|z|=1}|sum_l q_l z^l|^2; report exact fourth-moment tensor certificates and comparisons for N-of-1 carryover designs. Do not claim Wald inference, fixed treatment counts, or multi-arm applicability. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: exact LP enumeration for T=4–13 and construction checks through T=16 support the all-horizon parity formula; mirrored independent edge signs attain it; Golay covariance checks through length 256 support the stationary spectral limit. A disturbance spike refutes uniform Wald inference, and fixed counts violate the design class. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: prove the coefficient-level stationary Golay-block covariance with random-phase endpoints and the actual zero-prehistory estimator denominators, including the finite-state complexity bound. EARLY KILL TEST: exactly enumerate Golay blocks at lengths 8 and 16 for K=3,4, verify the boundary covariance/normalization identities, and reproduce the T=5 parity certificate; any failure stops the stationary theorem. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/exp_n1_chaos_optimal_design.md.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing N-of-1 work supplies the quadratic-chaos expansion but fixes independent assignment; the newest Markovian-design work restricts the design family and studies large-horizon OLS criteria; balanced temporal designs retain an approximation gap; and switchback results optimize another potential-outcome class. The prior CausalSmith projects expose parity-sensitive binary-moment geometry but only at the second-moment level. Here the risk depends on lagged fourth moments E[x_t x_{t-l} x_s x_{s-m}], so pairwise orthogonality does not determine it. For K=2, edge-sign dependence survives all second-moment constraints, while odd T obstructs the cancellation available for even T. The missing step is an exact description of the relevant fourth-moment face and a parity-sensitive algebraic dual.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An exact characterization establishing whether V_{T,2}=max{R_e^2,a_T R_g^2/T}, with a_T=1 for even T and 2 for odd T, together with necessary-and-sufficient optimizer membership conditions, explicit mirrored-edge-sign attaining laws, and matching primal-dual parity certificates.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames temporal dependence in assignment as the central design choice for estimating individual impulse responses and clearly separates structured implementable designs from the unresolved global optimum.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: N-of-1 trials estimate dynamic individual effects -> assignment dependence controls impulse-response precision -> existing analyses optimize structured Markov families asymptotically -> exact global fourth-order minimax randomization remains unresolved

method_exemplars.technique: Expand the moment estimator into linear disturbance and quadratic assignment-chaos components, then enumerate the fourth-moment configurations contributing to its MSE.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It analyzes the identical causal moment estimator; the independent-Rademacher tensor is precisely the proof component that must be replaced by the admissible correlated tensor.

method_exemplars.technique: Reduce temporal randomization risk using a least-favourable adversary and structural lemmas, then certify discrete optimality through a tight continuous relaxation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired parity result likewise requires matching lower and upper bounds for a discrete temporal assignment game.

method_exemplars.technique: Encode degree-four binary pseudomoments through a Gramian and derive positivity, consistency, and parity-sensitive restrictions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The unknown optimizer set is a projection of a degree-four ±1 moment body, so this supplies the closest geometric language for membership and separation.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Golay complementarity cancels correlations after summing two deterministic experiments, whereas a one-path causal experiment needs a single probability law with zero first moments, exact pairwise orthogonality, and a controlled fourth-moment tensor. Stationary Rudin-Shapiro calculations do not supply the random-phase finite-block endpoint law, actual zero-prehistory normalization, or finite-state complexity. Prior CausalSmith orbit-mixture and eigenvector lifts establish legal finite designs only for reduced second-moment or subset-lattice problems; they are not stationary and do not preserve the required lag-four tensor after phase randomization and concatenation. The first missing proof step is a coefficient-level block identity converting complementary autocorrelation into exact second- and fourth-order moments, including boundary coordinates.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A construction giving a finite-state random-phase Golay-block law, its complete second- and fourth-moment tensor, an explicit state-count bound, and an equality showing that its zero-prehistory estimator risk attains R_e^2 max_{|z|=1}|sum_l q_l z^l|^2 and the corresponding finite-horizon limit.

writing_exemplar.why: It makes correlated randomization a natural response to long-range dependence in individual impulse-response estimation without suggesting that sequence-design papers posed the causal problem.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Individual interventions have distributed effects -> independent toggling creates long-dependent quadratic-chaos error -> structured correlation may improve precision -> an implementable complementary-sequence law must attain the spectral benchmark

method_exemplars.technique: Use the complementary-pair polynomial recursion to cancel every nonzero aperiodic autocorrelation coefficient.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The target stationary value is spectral, and complementary-polynomial cancellation is the exact finite identity proposed to flatten the nuisance assignment spectrum.

method_exemplars.technique: Derive even-order Rudin-Shapiro correlations recursively and reduce four-point correlations to a finite system of arithmetic recurrences.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The causal estimator risk depends on exact fourth assignment moments, making these recurrences the nearest available tensor-calculation machinery.

method_exemplars.technique: Express impulse-response estimation error through Toeplitz autocorrelation matrices and exploit the constant eigenvalue sum of complementary inputs.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It directly connects complementary sequences to impulse-response MSE, but its repeated deterministic experiments must be replaced by one randomized causal path.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Covariance and Fisher-information relaxations cannot distinguish pairwise-orthogonal assignment laws having different fourth moments, even though the signal component of the causal moment estimator is quadratic in assignment. The generalized elliptope describes pseudomoments, not necessarily genuine path-law moments, and prior CausalSmith work obtains an exact parity boundary only on a two-block second-moment slice. The relevant object here additionally has Toeplitz lag indexing, repeated-index identities, shift consistency, finite-horizon boundary coordinates, and pairwise-zero constraints. Existing N-of-1 analyses either fix independence or restrict the Markov family and pass to large T. The concrete obstacle is to separate realizable lag tensors from positive-semidefinite pseudo-tensors and construct a dual polynomial that retains zero-prehistory boundary terms.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient membership characterization for the relevant lag-four tensor projection, with explicit orbit-mixture realizations and separating certificates, inducing equal-valued finite-dimensional primal and algebraic or semidefinite dual programs for every T,K,q plus an explicit convergence rate to the stationary spectral value.

writing_exemplar.why: It cleanly motivates assignment-law optimization for impulse-response targets and shows why tractable structured classes are used when the unrestricted temporal design problem is difficult.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Impulse-response precision depends on the temporal assignment law -> structured Markov designs make optimization tractable -> unrestricted pairwise-orthogonal laws differ through fourth moments -> exact tensor geometry is needed for global finite-horizon optimality

method_exemplars.technique: Represent degree-four ±1 pseudomoments by a Gramian and derive necessary-and-sufficient consistency and positivity constraints.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested primal variable is a projected degree-four binary tensor, and the proof must identify which generalized-elliptope constraints survive under lag projection.

method_exemplars.technique: Lift finite-time amplitude-constrained input design to a semidefinite moment problem and obtain dual upper bounds with randomized feasible recovery.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired characterization is another binary time-domain design lift, but exactness requires retaining fourth-order realizability rather than accepting the relaxation gap.

method_exemplars.technique: Write the estimator MSE as explicit linear-convolution and quadratic-chaos norms and compare finite linear convolution with its circular analogue.
method_exemplars.why_closest: These formulas provide the objective coefficients and isolate the zero-prehistory boundary terms that the proposed primal-dual certificate must preserve.

literature_map:
Liang and Recht (2025, Biometrika; arXiv:2310.16989) is the direct anchor: it gives an unbiased moment estimator for individual LTI impulse responses and derives its higher Rademacher moments under independent toggling.
Its discussion leaves balanced or more deliberate assignment designs open and links design improvement to shorter N-of-1 trials.
Guo and Liang (2026; arXiv:2606.28200) is the newest adjacent result: it optimizes Markovian random-switch and cycle-switch designs for finite-order impulse-response OLS targets and proves large-T structured-class results.
That paper does not characterize unrestricted sign-symmetric pairwise-orthogonal laws, exact finite-horizon fourth-moment risk, or the joint ellipsoidal adversary in this topic.
Ni, Bojinov, and Zhao (2022, NeurIPS Causal Dynamics Workshop) formulate minimax temporal design over assignment distributions, but their implementable balanced design is only a two-approximation.
Bojinov, Simchi-Levi, and Zhao (2023, Management Science; arXiv:2009.00148) solve regular-switchback minimax design through adversary reduction and continuous relaxation under bounded carryover potential outcomes.
Bojinov and Shephard (2019, JASA; arXiv:1706.07840) provide the design-based single-series causal-estimand baseline, including exact randomization tests.
Hu and Wager (arXiv:2209.00197) analyze switchbacks under geometric mixing, illustrating a stochastic temporal-dependence framework distinct from fixed-path ellipsoidal minimax risk.
Manchester (2010, IEEE CDC; arXiv:1009.5614) lifts amplitude-constrained system-identification input design to an SDP, but the general guarantee retains a relaxation gap.
Iannelli, Yin, and Smith (2021, IFAC SYSID; arXiv:2012.08126) optimize impulse-response MSE through signal-matrix input design under likelihood assumptions rather than design-based adversarial risk.
Golay (1961, IRE TIT; doi:10.1109/TIT.1961.1057620) supplies complementary binary pairs with zero summed nonzero aperiodic autocorrelation.
Tellambura, Guo, and Barton (1998, IEEE Communications Letters; doi:10.1109/4234.673660) connect complementary inputs to engineering impulse-response MSE, but use multiple deterministic inputs rather than one randomized causal path.
Mazáč (2024, Indagationes Mathematicae; arXiv:2211.01090) derives balanced Rudin-Shapiro multipoint correlations, including the closest available four-point tensor machinery.
Bandeira and Kunisky (2018; arXiv:1812.11583) characterize the degree-four generalized elliptope, while also showing why positive-semidefinite pseudomoments need not be moments of genuine binary laws.
The combined literature leaves unoccupied the exact finite-horizon fourth-order minimax problem, its parity faces, and a random-phase finite-state Golay construction with zero-prehistory boundary certificates.
